To draw the projections of the pentagonal pyramid:

1. **Draw the Top View:** 
   - Draw a regular pentagon with sides $30\text{ mm}$ such that one edge of the base is parallel to the V.P. 
   - Mark the center of the pentagon and join it with the corners to get the slant edges. Label the corners and the apex $o'$.

2. **Draw the Front View:** 
   - Project the base corners and the apex upwards to the $X-Y$ line. 
   - The base lies on the $X-Y$ line since the base is horizontal (resting on H.P.). 
   - The height of the axis is $65\text{ mm}$. Draw the front view as a triangle with base width equal to the projected pentagon width and height $65\text{ mm}$.

3. **Sectional Top View:** 
   - A horizontal section plane cuts the pyramid at a distance of $25\text{ mm}$ above the base. Draw a cutting plane line parallel to the $X-Y$ line at $25\text{ mm}$ height in the front view.
   - Project the intersection points of the section plane with the slant edges down to the corresponding slant edges in the top view.
   - Join these projected points to form a smaller similar pentagon. 
   - Hatch the region between the outer boundaries of the cut section to obtain the sectional top view.
proTip: Ensure that the cutting plane is shown as a thin chain line with thick ends in the front view, and hatch lines are uniformly spaced at $45^\circ$.
